program: Energy bill assistance, home efficiency and public energy-affordability access
priceScope: Conditional whole annual recipient cost against partial bill-assistance health and household-resource benefits; not whole-portfolio expected value or marginal gift price.

what: Energy Outreach Colorado helps income-qualified households pay utility bills and improves home energy efficiency and safety.
Its statewide 2025 household total covers several programs, so a bill-assistance subset and Denver share are explicit judgments.
The initial reference includes health and signed net household resources, including a distinct public or tariff-payer loss.
strengths: Current service, legal recipient and direct donation route are verified.
Original annual finances expose public and utility funding alongside cash assistance.
Clinical-null, financial-only, payer and cost-scope scenarios keep redistribution and health separate.
reservations: Reported households are not a deduplicated annual bill-assistance cohort.
LEAP, WAP and utility obligations are important alternatives rather than entirely donor-created benefits.
Clinical utility, net cash displacement, county residence and marginal gift expansion are unmeasured.

sections.what: Energy Outreach Colorado, EIN 74-2543881, provides bill payment, emergency furnace repairs, efficiency upgrades and advocacy statewide. Current 2026 outreach awards are supported by mandatory utility-customer charges and promote access to LEAP, WAP and EOC programs, not new household income equal to the grant amount.
sections.monitoring: The current homepage reports 40,789 households and 120,328 individuals served in 2025 across programs. These are not added together. Request unique bill-assistance households, repeated payments, county residence, disconnections avoided, indoor temperatures and net recipient/payer resource changes. The cumulative $410M invested since1989 is not an annual denominator.
sections.qualitative: The center assigns half of the reported household envelope to bill assistance, with .9 deduplication and .45 Denver share as judgments. Incremental benefit share .25 reflects public/utility alternatives; .2 clinical response, .01 utility and half-year persistence are hypotheses about temperature/security, not measured recipient QALYs. Furnace, efficiency, institutional and policy benefits outside this channel are unknown rather than zero.
sections.cost: Whole FYending September2025 recognized cost is $76,988,385, including $79,557 netted direct event costs. Bill-program cost $21,873,982 is a cost-aligned recognized-channel sensitivity, excluding allocated overhead and volunteer costs. Net household resource gain $500 is judged after benefit withdrawal and otherwise-paid bills, halved for positive overlap; $15 participation burden is charged to all exposed households. A distinct $150 payer loss per attributed household tests tariff/public incidence. No gross grant, retail energy value or ordinary survivor wages are treated as net welfare.
sections.funding: Original full expenses are FY2023 $65,890,165, FY2024 $83,135,058, FY2025 $76,988,385. Original period headers confirm these fiscal years. FY2025 government grants $14,090,961 and restricted efficiency/furnace programs mean general donations do not automatically expand all observed services. The current donation page redirects to an owned donor-support payment route; actual next-gift capacity requires recipient confirmation.

model.costScope: Whole statewide annual recipient cost against partial bill-assistance benefit reference; recognized bill-program sensitivity is not full social cost or marginal gift.
model.geographicAttribution: Pinned ten-county Denver CBSA19740; .45 household share judged given statewide service and no county output distribution.
model.formula: Exposed=N×channel×unique; incremental union=exposed×b; clinical people=union×response. Health=(clinical people×q×discounted finite duration−exposed×harm)×Denver share. Household joint-log net resources preserve full costs; distinct payer losses apply to the attributed union and local allocation once. Price=10C/(health+signed income equivalent).
model.counterfactual: LEAP, WAP, utility payment plans, mandated utility-charge assistance, other community providers and household support without added recipient work.
model.attribution: .25 incremental share, .5 bill-channel share and .9 deduplication are separate transparent judgments, not measured causal success.
model.uncertainty: Native program overlap, public replacement funding, actual disposable resources, clinical response/duration, payer incidence and local capacity remain uncertain.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 primary homepage: 40,789 households and120,328 individuals across programs. FY2025 original cash-assistance program cost21,873,982; no matched unique bill-cohort result.
